question: What is Schwab's strategy for its RIA custody business?

claims.text: Schwab has built its adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed, and continues to invest in the business to meet advisers' needs.

Schwab states (3Q26 transcript, October 2026) that the RIA custody business requires scale, trust, operational excellence, outstanding service, and breadth to support advisers as their businesses and clients' needs become more complex.

Schwab states (3Q25 transcript, October 2025) it is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs.

Schwab states in its 10-K (2025-12-31) that management believes it can maintain its competitive position primarily through the efforts of its sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients.

Schwab states (investor day deck, May 2026) that it aims to be the leading RIA support ecosystem, providing wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.
Schwab states (4Q24 transcript, January 2025) that in advisor services it is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while also helping new advisors transition to independence.

Schwab describes its offering (3Q26 deck, October 2026) as a differentiated, full-service platform built on scale and reputation, breadth beyond custody, operational excellence, and dedicated service and support.

Schwab (trade press, October 2026) will continue to focus on custody services for RIAs with under $100 million in AUM, positioning its role as providing a platform and support ecosystem to help advisors support clients and help their firms thrive.

Schwab (trade press, October 2026) wants to give RIAs equal or better access than their wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending, private market investing, and long-short investment strategies, positioning itself as the RIA's bank.
Schwab's strategic priorities (investor day deck, May 2026) include broadening support for RIAs while improving monetization.

Schwab states (10-K, Advisor Services segment) that it maintains its competitive position through sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed, with a focus on superior service and technology providing a highly-developed, scalable platform.

Schwab states (October 2026) its advisor business is built around helping independent advisors grow, compete and succeed, and that the business requires scale, trust, operational excellence, outstanding service and breadth.

Schwab states (3Q25 transcript, Advisor Services business) it is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms by building a broader support ecosystem beyond custody alone, including grown lending support, alternatives capability, and an expanded institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform.

Schwab states (May 2026) its priority is to provide the leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, with wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.
Schwab states (January 2025, advisor services) it is adding support and capabilities for RIAs of all sizes while helping new advisors transition to independence.

Schwab (trade press, October 2026) cites focus areas for its custody offerings as lending (pledged-asset lines), private-market investing, and long-short investment strategies, and playing the role of being RIAs' bank to help them manage both sides of clients' balance sheets.

Schwab (trade press, October 2026) will continue to focus on custody services for RIAs with under $100 million AUM, and states its role is to provide a platform and support ecosystem to help advisors support clients and thrive.
Schwab (4Q24 transcript, advisor services) states the opportunity going forward is to offer a more curated set of alternatives to advisors rather than primarily just custodying the assets.

Schwab (1Q26 transcript, Advisor Services) states it has rounded out its offering to advisors by adding more lending capabilities, including a structured asset lending program enabling clients to borrow against alternative and restricted/private shares.

Schwab (trade press, August 2026) states, as the largest custodian for advisors, it is focused on creating long-term value and access for advisors and on investing in innovation, capabilities, and service to help advisors grow and investors succeed.
Schwab's 10-K states that in the Advisor Services arena it competes with institutional custodians, wirehouses, regional and independent broker-dealers, fintech custodians, banks, and trust companies.
Fidelity Investments is named (trade press, October 2026) as the second-largest custodian after Schwab in the RIA custody business.
Fidelity is named (trade press, October 2026) as Schwab's close rival in cash/custody services.
Altruist is named (trade press, October 2026) as a Vanguard-owned custodian competing in the RIA custody space.
SEI, Goldman, and Robinhood are named (trade press, August 2026) as custodial alternatives that RIAs might consider as competitors to Schwab.
BNY Pershing is named (trade press, October 2026) as a custodian used alongside Schwab by breakaway RIA teams.
LPL is named (trade press, October 2026) as an independent broker/dealer and RIA custodian.
Vanguard, through its acquisition of Altruist, is named (trade press, August 2026) as a competitor that sets up to compete with Schwab in RIA custody.
Schwab (3Q26 transcript, October 2026) states that as of September 30, 2026 it serves more than 16,000 independent advisory firms on its platform (Advisor Services).
Schwab states these more than 16,000 firms represent $5.8 trillion in assets on its platform (Advisor Services), as of September 30, 2026.
Schwab (trade press, October 2026) added 1,001 new RIAs to its custody platform in Q3 2026, far more than its nearest peers (Advisor Services).
Schwab reports (3Q26 deck, October 2026) 1,101 custodians added to ADVs in 3Q26, versus peers adding 349, 339, 202, and 79.
Schwab (3Q26 transcript) reports that more than 1,100 advisory firms added Schwab as a custodian in 2025, more than 3x the next closest provider (Advisor Services).
Advisor Services client assets were $5,845.9 billion at September 30, 2026.
Advisor Services client assets were $5,741.9 billion at June 30, 2026.
Advisor Services client assets were $5,201.5 billion at March 31, 2026.
Advisor Services client assets were $5,195.5 billion at December 31, 2025.
Advisor Services client assets were $5,016.7 billion at September 30, 2025.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab announced (1Q25 transcript, March 2025) a strategic investment in wealth.com, described as one part of a broader effort to provide more of an ecosystem for its RIA clients to help them grow, compete, and succeed. Why it might matter: the source describes the investment as enhancing estate planning capabilities and experience for clients and as one part of the broader effort to help RIAs grow, compete, and succeed.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab (3Q25 transcript, September 2025) is deepening relationships with its 16,000 RIA firms by building a broader support ecosystem beyond custody alone, including grown lending support, expanded alternatives capability, an expanded institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform (funds from nearly 60 managers), and the launch of Advisor ProDirect. Why it might matter: the source frames this as driving growth by deepening relationships with clients, a first focus area.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab (3Q25 transcript, September 2025) supported the largest advisor transition in the history of its industry by welcoming OpenArc to its platform in September 2025. Why it might matter: the source describes this as supporting the largest advisor transition in the history of its industry.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab (4Q25 transcript, December 2025) is expanding its wealth services offer for Advisor Services, including its Model Market Center platform and alternative investments, expanding lending and trust services through Charles Schwab Bank, and delivering trading capabilities including a high-touch trading service for block trades launching in Q1. Why it might matter: the source describes this as a set of monetization opportunities providing value to clients across both Advisor Services and Retail.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab (1Q26 transcript, March 2026) launched a structured asset lending program enabling advisors' clients to borrow against alternative investments and restricted or private shares. Why it might matter: the source notes advisors had wanted and are now getting more lending capabilities.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab (3Q26 transcript, September 2026) collaborated with Anthropic and became the first RIA custodian included in Claude for Financial Advisors. Why it might matter: the source frames this as a continuing innovation across its businesses, alongside launches like the Charley AI assistant.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab (trade press, October 2026) plans to push bank capabilities for RIAs to compete with wirehouses, giving independent advisors equal or better access to banking services such as lending, private market investing, and long-short investment strategies. Why it might matter: the source notes Schwab CEO Rick Wurster cited growing pledged-asset lending balances, demand for long-short strategies, and the need to make private-market investing more accessible as focus areas.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab (trade press, October 2026) will continue to focus on its custody services for registered investment advisors with under $100 million in AUM. Why it might matter: the source notes the comments come after Fidelity Investments, the second-largest custodian after Schwab, told RIAs in early October 2026 that firms with under $100 million in client assets will have to leave its platform by June 30, 2027.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab (trade press, October 2026) is offering a $4,800 credit toward the Claude enterprise version to give smaller advisors access to AI connectors between Schwab Advisor Center and their own tools. Why it might matter: the source describes the credit as giving smaller advisors access to the AI connectors.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Syntax (trade press, October 2026) integrated its index engine with Schwab's iRebal platform to streamline direct indexing for RIAs, linking index creation, calculation, model management, trading and tax management support. Why it might matter: the source notes iRebal is Schwab's rebalancing platform acquired in its acquisition of the custodian TD Ameritrade.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab (trade press, November 2026) is partnering with Nevis, an AI operating system for wealth management, to offer a digital onboarding process for Schwab RIAs, and is moving exclusively to Docusign for executing agreements. Why it might matter: the source notes that going forward, advisors can no longer use paper forms and ink signatures.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab (trade press, October 2026) acquired Forge Global to broaden its private market capabilities (including access to pre-IPO companies), and later agreed to divest the Forge Trust self-directed IRA custodian business while keeping Forge's private markets platform. Why it might matter: the source notes Schwab completed the $660 million deal for Forge Global earlier that year and remains committed to Forge's private markets platform.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab (trade press, October 2026) is developing a proprietary long-short investment strategy to sustainably deliver long-short capabilities to its clients and RIAs. Why it might matter: the source notes Schwab and Fidelity have recently limited the use of long-short investment strategies to manage high demand.

The Charles Schwab Corporation: Schwab (1Q26 transcript, March 2026) is building its own books and records and custody capabilities as a prelude to offering clients choice in how they hold equities, and to support future tokenization of securities. Why it might matter: the source notes this builds optionality to support the future of tokenization should that be of interest to clients.

adjacent.text: Schwab has more than 3,000 employees dedicated to serving advisors (i.e., employees, not the advisors themselves), per trade press (October 2026).
adjacent.differs_because: These are counts of Schwab's own employees dedicated to serving advisors, not the advisor headcount of the RIA custody business (the independent RIA advisors whose firms custody with Schwab).

adjacent.text: Schwab noted (trade press, October 2026) it has some 3,000 financial advisors in-house (its own retail advice staff), many of whom hold CFPs.
adjacent.differs_because: These are counts of Schwab's in-house financial advisors (retail advice staff), not the advisor headcount of the RIA custody business (the independent RIA advisors whose firms custody with Schwab).
